cards.explanation: The answer is that he prays to the LORD. The text says, “So he prayed to the LORD, who spoke to him and gave him a sign.” (2 Chronicles 32:24) When my oven timer starts beeping in a weird way, I stand there and stare at it, and staring has never fixed one timer. Hezekiah took his problem to the right place.

The answer is True. Hezekiah prays, and the LORD "…spoke to him and gave him a sign." (2 Chronicles 32:24) The king is mortally ill, and he gets an answer. The text doesn't say here what the sign was, so I'm not going to make one up.

The answer is that his heart is proud. The text puts it plainly: "But because his heart was proud, Hezekiah did not repay the favor shown to him." (2 Chronicles 32:25) Pride is the reason the writer gives. Pride is sneaky like that, friends, because it can sit in a heart quietly and look like nothing.

The answer is Hezekiah and Judah and Jerusalem. The verse says "…wrath came upon him and upon Judah and Jerusalem." (2 Chronicles 32:25) It comes upon the king and upon the whole land together. That's a heavy line, so I'm going to let it sit for a second.

The answer is humbled. The text says, "Then Hezekiah humbled the pride of his heart…" (2 Chronicles 32:26). Pride was the problem, and humbling is what he does about it. I've humbled myself in front of a burnt batch before, friends, and it's a lot cheaper than pride.

The answer is False. The verse says, "Then Hezekiah humbled the pride of his heart—he and the people of Jerusalem…" (2 Chronicles 32:26). The king and the people of Jerusalem both do the humbling. So he isn't alone in it, and the people don't stay proud.

The answer is that the wrath does not come in Hezekiah's days. The text says they humbled themselves "…so that the wrath of the LORD did not come upon them during the days of Hezekiah." (2 Chronicles 32:26) The humbling and the wrath not coming are right there in the same verse. I'd call that a very good trade.

The answer is False. The verse says, "And Hezekiah prospered in all that he did." (2 Chronicles 32:30) Prospered is the word the text gives for everything he did, the building and the riches included. Struggling in most of it doesn't fit with that, friends. So the statement doesn't match what the verse says.

The answer is the wonder that happened in the land. The ambassadors "…were sent to him to inquire about the wonder that had happened in the land…" (2 Chronicles 32:31) That's what they came to ask about. The text doesn't spell out which wonder it means, so I'll leave it right there.

The answer is test. "…God left him alone to test him, that He might know all that was in Hezekiah’s heart." (2 Chronicles 32:31) Test is the word the text uses, friends. It also says what the test is for, which is all that was in Hezekiah's heart.

The answer is in the upper tombs of David's descendants. Hezekiah "…was buried in the upper tombs of David’s descendants." (2 Chronicles 32:33) David was Israel's king, and these tombs belong to his descendants. Hezekiah is laid to rest in those tombs.
The answer is True. "All Judah and the people of Jerusalem paid him honor at his death." (2 Chronicles 32:33) It says all Judah and the people of Jerusalem, friends. That's a big farewell.

The answer is his son Manasseh. The passage ends with "…his son Manasseh reigned in his place." (2 Chronicles 32:33) Manasseh is Hezekiah's son, and he takes the throne. The story of Hezekiah's reign closes here, but the story of the kings of Judah keeps going.
